headline: New England states select 102.4 MW in new solar projects
dek: Connecticut, Massachusetts and Rhode Island chose four projects in New Hampshire and Maine through a coordinated procurement aimed at adding power and containing regional energy costs.
body: Connecticut, Massachusetts and Rhode Island have selected four new solar projects totaling 102.4 megawatts through a coordinated procurement for zero-carbon electricity, the Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection announced Thursday.

Connecticut is taking 63.4 megawatts from three projects: the 30-megawatt Keene Meadow Solar Station in Keene, New Hampshire, a 17-megawatt West Baldwin project in Baldwin, Maine, and a 16.4-megawatt Emery Meadow project in Buxton, Maine. Rhode Island selected 20 megawatts from Keene Meadow, while Massachusetts selected 19 megawatts from the Saco Solar project in Saco, Maine.

The states said the portfolio is expected to produce about 190,000 megawatt-hours of electricity each year. Connecticut officials said their share would be equivalent to the annual electricity use of more than 22,000 homes, while the broader procurement is intended to add supply, improve grid reliability and reduce energy and capacity-market costs for New England ratepayers.

The solicitation was coordinated with Maine and Vermont as well as the three purchasing states. The selected projects must begin delivering electricity by the end of 2032; Connecticut is still evaluating nuclear proposals submitted through the same request for proposals and plans to announce those decisions later.
